title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 32 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 32 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 32 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 32.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 32, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Sennacherib king of Assyria came and encamped against the fenced cities
Hezekiah stopped the waters of the fountains outside the city
Hezekiah built up the broken wall and repaired Millo
Sennacherib sent servants to Jerusalem with a message
questions.correctAnswer: Sennacherib king of Assyria came and encamped against the fenced cities
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:1 states that after these things, Sennacherib king of Assyria came and encamped against the fenced cities. This is the first event mentioned in the chapter.

questions.question: Who was the king of Assyria that came into Judah?
options: Nebuchadnezzar
Sennacherib
Tiglath-Pileser
Ashurbanipal
questions.correctAnswer: Sennacherib
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:1 specifically names Sennacherib as the king of Assyria who came into Judah.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah do when he saw that Sennacherib was come and purposed to fight Jerusalem?
options: He fled the city
He took counsel with his princes and mighty men to stop the waters of the fountains outside the city
He surrendered to Sennacherib
He sent gifts to Sennacherib
questions.correctAnswer: He took counsel with his princes and mighty men to stop the waters of the fountains outside the city
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:2-3 shows that Hezekiah took counsel with his princes and mighty men to stop the waters of the fountains which were without the city.

questions.question: Why did the people stop all the fountains and the brook running through the land?
options: To prepare for planting crops
To keep the Assyrian kings from finding much water
To create a moat around the city
To irrigate the city gardens
questions.correctAnswer: To keep the Assyrian kings from finding much water
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:4 states that the people stopped all the fountains and the brook saying, 'Why should the kings of Assyria come, and find much water?'

questions.question: What did Hezekiah build and repair to strengthen the city?
options: A palace and stables
All the broken wall, towers, another wall without, and Millo in the city of David
A large temple
A new gate for the city
questions.correctAnswer: All the broken wall, towers, another wall without, and Millo in the city of David
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:5 describes that Hezekiah strengthened himself, built up the broken wall, raised it to the towers, built another wall without, and repaired Millo.

questions.question: What weapons did Hezekiah make in abundance?
options: Swords and helmets
Darts and shields
Bows and arrows
Spears and armor
questions.correctAnswer: Darts and shields
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:5 specifically mentions that Hezekiah made darts and shields in abundance.

questions.question: Where did Hezekiah gather the people to speak comfortably to them?
options: In the temple
In the street of the gate of the city
On the city wall
In the king's palace
questions.correctAnswer: In the street of the gate of the city
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:6 states that Hezekiah gathered the people in the street of the gate of the city to speak comfortably to them.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah tell the people regarding fear of the king of Assyria and his multitude?
options: To surrender immediately
Be strong and courageous, do not be afraid nor dismayed
To flee the city
To negotiate peace
questions.correctAnswer: Be strong and courageous, do not be afraid nor dismayed
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:7 records Hezekiah telling the people to be strong and courageous, not afraid nor dismayed of the king of Assyria or his multitude.

questions.question: According to Hezekiah, who is with them to help fight their battles?
options: The king of Egypt
The LORD our God
Their own armies
The neighboring tribes
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD our God
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:8 says that with them is the LORD their God to help and fight their battles.

questions.question: What did Sennacherib do while he sent his servants to Jerusalem?
options: Laid siege against Lachish with all his power
Marched to Egypt
Built a new fortress
Retreated from Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Laid siege against Lachish with all his power
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:9 states that Sennacherib laid siege against Lachish with all his power while sending his servants to Jerusalem.

questions.question: What did Sennacherib ask the people of Jerusalem regarding their trust?
options: Whereon do ye trust, that ye abide in the siege in Jerusalem?
Who will help you in battle?
Will you join forces with Assyria?
Do you have enough food for the siege?
questions.correctAnswer: Whereon do ye trust, that ye abide in the siege in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:10 records Sennacherib asking the people where they trust that they abide in the siege in Jerusalem.

questions.question: Sennacherib accused Hezekiah of persuading the people to give over themselves to die by famine and thirst.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:11 says Sennacherib asked if Hezekiah did not persuade them to give over themselves to die by famine and thirst.

questions.question: Hezekiah gathered captains of war to strengthen the people and spoke comforting words to them.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:6-8 shows Hezekiah set captains of war over the people and spoke comfortably to them encouraging courage.

questions.question: Hezekiah sent gifts to Sennacherib to try to make peace.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not mention Hezekiah sending gifts to Sennacherib; rather, he prepared the city for defense (2 Chronicles 32:1-8).

questions.question: Sennacherib personally led the siege against Jerusalem while sending servants to Lachish.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:9 states Sennacherib sent servants to Jerusalem but he himself laid siege against Lachish, not Jerusalem.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 32 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 32 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 32:12, what did Hezekiah command Judah and Jerusalem regarding worship?
options: Ye shall worship before one altar, and burn incense upon it
Ye shall worship idols in every city
Ye shall build many altars and burn incense on them
Ye shall not worship at all
questions.correctAnswer: Ye shall worship before one altar, and burn incense upon it
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:12 clearly states that Hezekiah commanded Judah and Jerusalem to worship before one altar and burn incense upon it.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 32:15 promise will happen if the people do not believe Hezekiah's message in 2 Chronicles 32:14?
options: Their God shall not deliver them out of the king of Assyria's hand
They will be victorious without any help
They will receive riches and peace
They will be healed of all diseases
questions.correctAnswer: Their God shall not deliver them out of the king of Assyria's hand
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:15 warns that no god of any nation was able to deliver his people out of the king of Assyria's hand, so if the people do not believe Hezekiah, their God will not deliver them.

questions.question: What reasoning does the king of Assyria give in 2 Chronicles 32:13 to challenge the power of Judah's God?
options: The gods of the nations were unable to deliver their lands from my hand
The people of Judah have no weapons to fight
Hezekiah has no authority over the people
The walls of Jerusalem are weak
questions.correctAnswer: The gods of the nations were unable to deliver their lands from my hand
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:13 contains the king of Assyria's claim that the gods of other nations could not deliver their lands from his hand, questioning why Judah's God would be any different.

questions.question: How do 2 Chronicles 32:16 and 2 Chronicles 32:17 together describe the actions of the king of Assyria's servants?
options: They spoke against the LORD God and Hezekiah, and wrote letters to rail against the God of Israel
They praised the God of Israel and Hezekiah publicly
They built altars in Jerusalem
They surrendered to Hezekiah's army
questions.correctAnswer: They spoke against the LORD God and Hezekiah, and wrote letters to rail against the God of Israel
questions.explanation: Verses 16 and 17 describe the servants speaking against the LORD God and Hezekiah, and also writing letters to insult the God of Israel.

questions.question: What practical lesson can believers learn from Hezekiah and Isaiah's response to the threats in 2 Chronicles 32:20?
options: Prayer and seeking God in times of crisis is essential
Ignoring problems will make them go away
Military strength alone guarantees victory
Deception is a valid tactic in conflict
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer and seeking God in times of crisis is essential
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:20 shows Hezekiah and Isaiah praying and crying to heaven, teaching believers to turn to God in difficult times.

questions.question: How does the king of Assyria try to intimidate the people of Jerusalem according to 2 Chronicles 32:18?
options: By crying with a loud voice in the Jews' speech to affright and trouble them
By sending gifts and peace offerings
By building walls around Jerusalem
By withdrawing his army
questions.correctAnswer: By crying with a loud voice in the Jews' speech to affright and trouble them
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:18 states that the king of Assyria's servants cried out loudly in the Jews' language to frighten and trouble the people of Jerusalem.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 32:19 imply about the nature of false gods compared to the God of Jerusalem?
options: False gods are the work of human hands and powerless
False gods are more powerful than the God of Jerusalem
False gods can protect cities better
False gods do not exist
questions.correctAnswer: False gods are the work of human hands and powerless
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:19 explicitly describes the gods of other peoples as made by human hands, implying their inability to protect people unlike the God of Jerusalem.

questions.question: What was the outcome of the LORD sending an angel according to 2 Chronicles 32:21?
options: The angel cut off the mighty men and leaders in the Assyrian camp, leading to the king's shameful return
The angel destroyed the walls of Jerusalem
The angel brought famine to Judah
The angel caused Hezekiah to surrender
questions.correctAnswer: The angel cut off the mighty men and leaders in the Assyrian camp, leading to the king's shameful return
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:21 describes how the LORD sent an angel who killed the king of Assyria's warriors and leaders, forcing him to return with shame.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 32:22, how did the LORD guide the inhabitants of Jerusalem after saving them?
options: He guided them on every side
He sent them into exile
He caused them to rebuild Assyria
He left them to fend for themselves
questions.correctAnswer: He guided them on every side
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:22 states that the LORD saved the inhabitants of Jerusalem and guided them on every side, indicating comprehensive protection.

questions.question: What practical encouragement does Hezekiah give to his people in 2 Chronicles 32:7 amidst the Assyrian siege?
options: Be strong and courageous, do not be afraid because God is with us
Flee the city immediately
Surrender to the king of Assyria
Hide and avoid all conflict
questions.correctAnswer: Be strong and courageous, do not be afraid because God is with us
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:7 records Hezekiah encouraging the people to be strong and courageous, not afraid or dismayed, because God would help fight their battles.

questions.question: How did Hezekiah prepare Jerusalem's defenses as described in 2 Chronicles 32:5?
options: He built up broken walls, raised towers, repaired the Millo, and made darts and shields in abundance
He tore down the walls of the city
He sent the people away from the city
He relied solely on prayer without physical defense
questions.correctAnswer: He built up broken walls, raised towers, repaired the Millo, and made darts and shields in abundance
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:5 details Hezekiah's efforts to strengthen Jerusalem physically by repairing walls and making weapons.

questions.question: What reason does Hezekiah give in 2 Chronicles 32:8 for why the people should not fear the Assyrians?
options: Because the LORD our God is with us to help and fight our battles
Because the Assyrians are few in number
Because the city walls are impenetrable
Because the Assyrians have no weapons
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD our God is with us to help and fight our battles
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:8 states that Hezekiah told the people not to fear because God was with them to help and fight their battles.

questions.question: What does the king of Assyria claim in 2 Chronicles 32:11 about Hezekiah's persuasion?
options: Hezekiah persuades you to give over yourselves to die by famine and thirst, trusting in the LORD
Hezekiah persuades you to attack Assyria
Hezekiah persuades you to make peace with Assyria
Hezekiah persuades you to abandon the city
questions.correctAnswer: Hezekiah persuades you to give over yourselves to die by famine and thirst, trusting in the LORD
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 32:11, the king of Assyria accuses Hezekiah of persuading the people to surrender to death by famine and thirst, relying on the LORD for deliverance.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Chronicles 32:14, no god of the nations that Sennacherib's fathers destroyed could deliver their people from his hand.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:14 states that none of the gods of the nations destroyed by Sennacherib's fathers could deliver their people from his hand.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Chronicles 32:22 says that the LORD saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants but did not provide guidance afterward.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:22 states that the LORD saved the inhabitants and guided them on every side, so it is false that guidance was not provided.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 32 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 32.

questions.question: What was the result of many bringing gifts to the LORD and presents to Hezekiah king of Judah?
options: He was magnified in the sight of all nations from thenceforth
He became wealthy beyond measure
Hezekiah built a temple for the LORD
The Assyrians retreated from Judah
questions.correctAnswer: He was magnified in the sight of all nations from thenceforth
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:23 states that many brought gifts unto the LORD and presents to Hezekiah so that he was magnified in the sight of all nations from then on.

questions.question: What sign did the LORD give to Hezekiah when he prayed during his sickness?
options: The shadow on the sundial moved backward
An angel struck down the Assyrians
Hezekiah's illness was completely healed
The waters of Gihon were stopped
questions.correctAnswer: The shadow on the sundial moved backward
questions.explanation: Though 2 Chronicles 32:24 mentions Hezekiah was sick and prayed and the LORD gave him a sign, the sign of the shadow moving backward is recorded in 2 Kings 20:8-11, a direct cross-reference and fulfillment of this verse.

questions.question: Why did wrath come upon Hezekiah, Judah, and Jerusalem after his recovery?
options: Because Hezekiah's heart was lifted up and he did not render according to the benefit done unto him
Because Hezekiah stopped the waters of Gihon
Because Hezekiah refused to pay tribute to Assyria
Because the people worshiped idols again
questions.correctAnswer: Because Hezekiah's heart was lifted up and he did not render according to the benefit done unto him
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:25 explains that Hezekiah did not return according to the benefit done unto him, his heart was lifted up, and therefore wrath came upon him, Judah, and Jerusalem.

questions.question: How was the wrath of the LORD avoided during Hezekiah's reign despite his pride?
options: Hezekiah humbled himself and so did the inhabitants of Jerusalem
Hezekiah built more storehouses
Hezekiah defeated the Assyrians by military force alone
Hezekiah formed an alliance with Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: Hezekiah humbled himself and so did the inhabitants of Jerusalem
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:26 shows that Hezekiah humbled himself for the pride of his heart, as did the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so the wrath of the LORD did not come upon them in his days.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT listed among Hezekiah's riches and honors?
options: Treasuries for silver and gold
Precious stones and spices
Chariots and horses
Shields and pleasant jewels
questions.correctAnswer: Chariots and horses
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:27 lists treasures for silver, gold, precious stones, spices, shields, and pleasant jewels but does not mention chariots and horses among Hezekiah's riches.

questions.question: What was the purpose of stopping the upper watercourse of Gihon and bringing it to the west side of the city of David?
options: To secure water supply for Jerusalem during a siege
To irrigate the fields outside the city
To create a defensive moat
To celebrate the feast of booths
questions.correctAnswer: To secure water supply for Jerusalem during a siege
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:30 describes how Hezekiah stopped the upper watercourse of Gihon and brought it to the west side of the city of David, which was a strategic move to ensure water supply inside Jerusalem during Assyrian threats.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'chazaq' (חָזַק) in 2 Chronicles 32:7 mean?
options: Be strong and courageous
Be humble and meek
Pray earnestly
Build walls quickly
questions.correctAnswer: Be strong and courageous
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 32:7, Hezekiah encourages the people using the Hebrew word 'chazaq,' which means 'be strong and courageous,' emphasizing steadfastness in the face of danger.

questions.question: Which literary device is most evident in 2 Chronicles 32:8 where Hezekiah contrasts 'an arm of flesh' with 'the LORD our God'?
options: Antithesis
Chiasm
Parallelism
Metaphor
questions.correctAnswer: Antithesis
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:8 uses antithesis by contrasting 'an arm of flesh' with 'the LORD our God,' highlighting the difference between human power and divine help.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of divine deliverance in the face of overwhelming human opposition found in 2 Chronicles 32:21?
options: Romans 8:31
Hebrews 11:32-34
Revelation 12:7-9
questions.explanation: Acts 12:6-11 recounts the miraculous deliverance of Peter from prison by an angel, echoing the theme of God sending an angel to destroy enemies as in 2 Chronicles 32:21.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects with Hezekiah's prayer and the Lord's response in 2 Chronicles 32:24?
options: Isaiah 38:1-8
Psalm 23
Exodus 14:21-22
Daniel 6:16-23
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 38:1-8
questions.explanation: Isaiah 38:1-8 records Hezekiah's sickness, prayer, and the sign God gave him, directly connecting with 2 Chronicles 32:24.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes the account of many bringing gifts to Hezekiah and the LORD in 2 Chronicles 32:23?
options: The LORD sending an angel to defeat the Assyrians
Hezekiah stopping the waters of Gihon
Hezekiah's sickness and prayer
Sennacherib's siege of Lachish
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD sending an angel to defeat the Assyrians
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:21-22 describe the LORD sending an angel to slay the Assyrian army, leading to the deliverance of Jerusalem, which precedes verse 23 where gifts are brought.

questions.question: How does the chapter use typology in the story of Hezekiah's deliverance from Assyria?
options: Hezekiah is a type of Christ as a righteous king who delivers his people
Hezekiah typifies the wicked king who opposes God
The Assyrian army symbolizes the New Testament church
The watercourse of Gihon represents the Holy Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: Hezekiah is a type of Christ as a righteous king who delivers his people
questions.explanation: Hezekiah's deliverance and prayer prefigure Christ as the righteous king who intercedes and delivers his people, a classic typology in biblical literature.

questions.question: What is the significance of God 'leaving' Hezekiah during the inquiry of the Babylonian ambassadors in 2 Chronicles 32:31?
options: It was a test to reveal the true condition of Hezekiah's heart
God abandoned Hezekiah permanently at this time
It meant immediate punishment would come upon Judah
It showed that Babylon would conquer Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: It was a test to reveal the true condition of Hezekiah's heart
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:31 explains that God left Hezekiah to try him and to know all that was in his heart, indicating a test rather than abandonment.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 32:33, what honor was given to Hezekiah after his death?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:33 states that Hezekiah was buried in the chiefest of the sepulchres of the sons of David and that all Judah and Jerusalem honored him at his death.

questions.question: Hezekiah's heart was never lifted up after he received the LORD's sign during his sickness. True or False?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:25 states that Hezekiah's heart was lifted up after the benefit done to him, which caused wrath upon him, Judah, and Jerusalem.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 32 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 32 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 32:8 teach about God's nature?
options: God is a helper and warrior for His people
God is indifferent to human affairs
God requires human strength alone for victory
God works only through natural means
questions.correctAnswer: God is a helper and warrior for His people
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:8 states, 'With him is an arm of flesh; but with us is the LORD our God to help us, and to fight our battles,' demonstrating God's active role as helper and warrior.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin does 2 Chronicles 32:25 teach?
options: Pride leads to divine wrath
Sin has no consequences for kings
God ignores human arrogance
Faith alone removes all judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Pride leads to divine wrath
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:25 states that Hezekiah's heart was lifted up and therefore wrath came upon him and Judah, illustrating the doctrine that pride brings God's judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning salvation is taught in 2 Chronicles 32:21?
options: God saves His people supernaturally from enemies
Salvation depends solely on military strength
Human wisdom alone secures deliverance
God allows His people to be defeated to teach humility
questions.correctAnswer: God saves His people supernaturally from enemies
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 32:21 describes God sending an angel to destroy the Assyrian army, showing that deliverance is by divine intervention, not human effort.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 32:22 specifically demonstrate?
options: Sovereignty
Immutability
Omniscience
Omnipresence
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Verse 22 shows that the LORD 'saved Hezekiah... and guided them on every side,' demonstrating God's sovereign control over events.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in 2 Chronicles 32:24?
options: Omnipotence
Revelation
Justice
Jealousy
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation
questions.explanation: God spoke to Hezekiah and gave him a sign (2 Chronicles 32:24), demonstrating His attribute of revealing His will to humans.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 32:1-5 connect to the theme of divine protection in the Pentateuch?
options: It shows God preserving His people behind fortified walls reminiscent of the Exodus protection
It replaces God's protection with human military might
It teaches that water is irrelevant to God's care
It contradicts the protection theme by emphasizing human strength
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God preserving His people behind fortified walls reminiscent of the Exodus protection
questions.explanation: The preparation of water supplies and fortifications reflects God's provision and protection themes seen in Exodus, where God defends Israel from enemies (2 Chronicles 32:1-5).

questions.question: In what way does 2 Chronicles 32:20-21 prepare for the New Testament theme of salvation by divine intervention?
options: It anticipates salvation by God's direct action rather than human effort
It emphasizes human battle tactics over divine help
It denies any need for prayer in salvation
It promotes military alliance as the primary means of salvation
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates salvation by God's direct action rather than human effort
questions.explanation: The LORD sending an angel to defeat Assyria (32:21) and the prayer of Hezekiah and Isaiah (32:20) prefigure salvation by divine power, a key New Testament doctrine.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 Chronicles 32:7 and 32:8 teach about faith and divine help?
options: Faith in God empowers courage because God fights battles for His people
Faith is irrelevant; human strength suffices
Divine help is conditional on military success alone
Fear of enemies is justified even with faith
questions.correctAnswer: Faith in God empowers courage because God fights battles for His people
questions.explanation: Verse 7 exhorts courage 'be not afraid,' and verse 8 states 'with us is the LORD our God to help us,' combining faith with divine empowerment for courage.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 Chronicles 32:25 and 32:26 teach about sin, repentance, and divine wrath?
options: Pride incurs wrath, but repentance can avert God's judgment
Sin has no effect on divine favor
Repentance is unnecessary for kings
God's wrath is inevitable regardless of repentance
questions.correctAnswer: Pride incurs wrath, but repentance can avert God's judgment
questions.explanation: Verse 25 speaks of wrath due to pride, while verse 26 shows humility prevented wrath, teaching repentance's power to avert judgment.

questions.question: What combined theological insight do 2 Chronicles 32:13 and 32:14 provide about the nature of God's power compared to pagan gods?
options: God's power is unique and superior to idols, who cannot deliver
All gods have equal power to save nations
Pagan gods deliver more effectively than the LORD
Idols are as powerful as the God of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God's power is unique and superior to idols, who cannot deliver
questions.explanation: Verses 13-14 emphasize that no gods of other nations could deliver from Assyria's hand, highlighting the unique and superior power of Israel's God.

questions.question: What combined doctrine is taught by 2 Chronicles 32:20 and 32:24 regarding the role of prayer and divine revelation in crisis?
options: Prayer calls upon God who responds with revelation and deliverance
Prayer is ineffective without signs
God reveals nothing in times of distress
Divine revelation replaces the need for prayer
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer calls upon God who responds with revelation and deliverance
questions.explanation: Verse 20 shows Hezekiah and Isaiah praying, and verse 24 shows God speaking and giving a sign, teaching that prayer prompts divine revelation and deliverance.

questions.question: Sceptics claim 2 Chronicles 32:20-22 teaches that God arbitrarily kills enemies and overrides human freedom. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God sovereignly delivers His people in response to prayer, demonstrating His power over hostile forces
God randomly kills without reason or prayer
Human freedom is negated and God forces outcomes without cause
The passage endorses violence as a means to power
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly delivers His people in response to prayer, demonstrating His power over hostile forces
questions.explanation: Verses 20-22 show Hezekiah and Isaiah praying and God sending an angel to defeat the enemy, indicating divine sovereignty and response to prayer, not arbitrary violence.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification does 2 Chronicles 32:3-4 teach?
options: Practical obedience includes preparing and trusting God by prudent measures
Sanctification is solely spiritual with no practical actions
Obedience ignores physical preparations
Faith excludes any human responsibility
questions.correctAnswer: Practical obedience includes preparing and trusting God by prudent measures
questions.explanation: Hezekiah's halting of waters (verses 3-4) shows that sanctification involves both trusting God and wise practical preparation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly evident in 2 Chronicles 32:31 in relation to God's testing of Hezekiah?
options: Omniscience
Impunity
Vindictiveness
Indifference
questions.correctAnswer: Omniscience
questions.explanation: Verse 31 says God left Hezekiah to try him to 'know all that was in his heart,' demonstrating God's omniscience in testing and knowing human hearts.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 32:27-29 contribute to the biblical understanding of God’s blessing and stewardship?
options: God blesses with material wealth which is to be stewarded responsibly
Material wealth is a sign of divine disfavor
God forbids accumulating earthly treasures
Blessing is unrelated to stewardship
questions.correctAnswer: God blesses with material wealth which is to be stewarded responsibly
questions.explanation: Verses 27-29 describe Hezekiah's great riches and possessions as blessings from God, implying the responsibility of stewardship.
